title: Function calling parse debug scratchpad (Ashwin)
body:
Goal:
- Triage intermittent parsing failures when agent/function tooling returns mal-formed JSON or unexpected types.
- Repro steps, hypothesis, commands tried, errors, and next actions.

Background / quick summary:
- Users (and internal e2e tests) occasionally see JSON parse errors when using tool/function calling (structured outputs). Failure rate ~0.3% in CI runs; in prod we saw 2 incidents last month (one customer report).
- Failures mostly occur when model returns trailing commas, stray text, or uses single quotes. Also seen: partial JSON + "more text" appended (model hallucination of extra commentary).

Repro (local):
1) Minimal prompt that triggers: ask assistant to return a tool call payload with strict JSON schema (fields: id:int, name:str, items:list[str]).
2) Run with local dev server (model=llama-3-small debug run).

Commands tried:
- curl to hosted debug endpoint (replicating client):
  curl -X POST \\n    -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \\n    -d '{"prompt":"return tool payload as JSON: {\\\"id\\\": 1, \\\"name\\\": \\\"x\\\", \\\"items\\\": [\\\"a\\\"]}"}' \\n    http://localhost:8080/v1/debug/generate

- python quick-run using our sdk: (snippet)
  from rdw_sdk import Client
  c = Client(local=True)
  r = c.generate(prompt=my_prompt, function_schema=my_schema, validate=True)
  print(r.text)

Observed errors / example traces:
- JSONDecodeError: Expecting property name enclosed in double quotes: line 1 column 3 (char 2)
  raw model output: "{ 'id': 1, 'name': 'foo', 'items': ['a', 'b'], }"

- Partial payload + extra: 
  raw model output: "{\"id\": 12, \"name\": \"x\", \"items\": [\"a\"] }\n  Note: sent from prompt A, ignore previous..."
  -> our strict parser fails on trailing newline + text after JSON.

- Trailing comma example:
  "{\"id\": 1, \"name\": \"x\", \"items\": [\"a\",], }"

Hypotheses:
- Model sometimes emits python/JS-like representation (single quotes) or human commentary appended.
- Temperature/sampling settings and few-shot examples influence tendency to append commentary.
- Our parser is too strict for downstream tolerant parsing (we use a strict json.loads). We should attempt a safe pre-clean pass.

Commands / experiments run so far (results):
- Experiment A: Pre-clean heuristic that strips trailing non-JSON text by finding first closing brace (}) and truncating after matched braces.
  - Result: fixed ~55% of CI failures but created false positives: truncated if JSON embedded in text (rare).
- Experiment B: Try single-quote replacement -> naive replace('\'','\"') then json.loads.
  - Result: fixed some cases but broke when apostrophes present in strings.
- Experiment C: Use regex to detect JSON block (first '{' to last '}' balanced) and feed to json5 parser (js-style tolerant).
  - Result: json5 handled trailing commas & single quotes. Reduced error rate to ~0.1% in local tests. Concern: security (json5 accepts comments) and silent acceptance of unexpected shapes.

Logs / snippets:
- CI log (2025-01-07):
  "FAIL: test_tool_parsing (tests.test_functions)\n   Traceback (most recent call last):\n     File \"tests/test_functions.py\", line 128, in test_tool_parsing\n       payload = strict_parse(r.text, schema)\n   json.decoder.JSONDecodeError: Expecting value: line 1 column 2 (char 1)\n  raw: \"\\'{'id': 1, 'name': 'x'}\\'\""

Notes to self / ideas:
- Prefer layered approach: try strict json.loads first -> if fails, attempt sanitized passes in order: 1) trim trailing non-json, 2) attempt json5, 3) fallback to regex extraction of top-level object, 4) as last resort return error with raw payload and hint to user for manual fix.
- Track metrics: count failures by failure-mode (single-quotes, trailing-text, trailing-commas, partial), include model, prompt-template id, temperature. Add to observability console as separate error buckets.
- Update e2e tests with adversarial templates that exercise these modes.

Open questions / risks:
- Should we auto-fix single quotes? Could change semantics for contractions/strings with apostrophes. Need tests.
- json5 acceptance could mask deeper schema mismatches (e.g., comments obscuring missing required fields). We still need robust schema validation post-parse.
- For Private deployments: we cannot rely on third-party json5 if customers restrict deps. Consider implementing small tolerant parser in-house (safer/easier to audit).

Next steps / TODOs:
- [ ] Add metric tags for each failure mode and ship to console (priority P1).
- [ ] Add an integration test that runs model variants (gpt-like, llama) with adversarial prompts (P0).
- [ ] Prototype layered parser in runtime: strict -> sanitize -> json5 fallback (P2).
- [ ] Create PR template to include raw model output when opening bugs (to help diagnose).
- [ ] Sync with Maya (SRE) and Jon (SDK) about acceptable sanitizer behavior (meeting planned 2025-01-12).

Scratchpad / quick heuristics tried (notes):
- naive_trim = re.sub(r"\\A.*?(\\{)", "\\1", s, flags=re.S)  # try to drop leading chatter
- find matching braces: walk chars, increment/decrement -> return substring 0..i when count==0
- json5.loads(s) guarded by max size and explicit deny patterns (no __proto__ etc)

Slack refs:
- #dev-tools thread: posted sample outputs 2025-01-09 (link above).

If I forget later:
- Key ticket: INF-3421 (parsing incident tracking)
- Local repro saved: /home/ashwin/tmp/parse-repros/2025-01-09/ (contains failing raw outputs)

-- Ashwin
